label: copy-phase input c early in the readback (sparse, context-gated)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). About 65% of activation mass is on input token c, mostly during the copy phase when c is fed back early in the readback (recall_idx 1-2, to_go >= 3, longer L; first_tok=c gives 12x lift). The strongest activations are at step L+1 after <DEL> when c is the first original token. Activation is stronger when the next token to output is c/o/j/3/2, but this only partly explains it. The feature fires on only a small fraction (about 3.5%) of copy-phase c inputs, so it depends on hidden-state context that no tested predicate captured (the best conjunction reached F1 about 0.27). A smaller share (about 30% of mass) comes from the original phase at steps 3-8 on mixed tokens (i, l, 2, 0, d), often in sequences that start with c. It almost never fires at t<3, at the delimiter, or for L<=4. Magnitudes are low (max 0.225) and roughly uniform.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=10: c, 2, t, j; t=9: c, 2, t, j; t=11: c, 2, j, t) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: c, j, 3, o; delimiter step: c, z, 3; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=7 & t=6, L=9 & t=13, L=8 & t=9.
